By combining Multimodal OCR and Neural Machine Translation (NMT) systems, methodology enables seamless recognition and translation of text into contemporary languages with spoken output. Overcoming accuracy challenges and linguistic nuances specific to historical manuscripts, the system enhances inclusivity for researchers and enthusiasts. The Multimodal OCR ensures adaptability to diverse manuscript formats, while the NMT guarantees precise translations. The inclusion of intelligent agents enhances system responsiveness, optimizing real-time processing. The integration of spoken output further broadens accessibility, cultivating a more inclusive and enriched experience for a diverse audience.

Author Keywords: Optical Character Recognition with intelligent agents

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Different Ingress Controllers Within the Kubernetes Cluster
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: The demand for effective and adaptable traffic routing systems has significantly increased as businesses use container orchestration platforms like Kubernetes. By addressing Kubernetes' intrinsic restrictions on external access, Ingress Controller helps to provide a more reliable, secure, and controllable infrastructure for containerised applications. In Kubernetes, the problem of traffic routing and external access for services inside a cluster is handled by an Ingress Controller. It serves as a specialized layer that controls incoming traffic, offering a declarative and centralized method for load balancing, creating routing rules, and making services visible to the public. The study examines many types of ingress controllers that are out there, each with unique characteristics and functionalities, such as NGNIX, HAProxy, Istio, Traefik and customized ingress controllers. In order for the user to determine which ingress controller will effectively meet the needs of the applications, the study compares a few ingress controllers from the various ingress controller categories based on the features they offer, service response time, and throughput performance.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition Using Focal Network and Resnet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: Image emotion recognition involves finding the emotions from visual data, usually done through convolutional neural networks (CNN) or deep neural networks (DNN). The existing methodologies are often high complex or time complex and it is not giving the good considerable results and computationally expensive due to high number of parameters. In this paper we try to accomplish a better output by using focal network which stood among other transformers architecture due to the unique property of the dynamic attention Recent studies have shown the efficacy of transformer architectures in various deep learning tasks and challenged the convolution neural networks on various tasks. but, It has a tradeoff between reduced parameter complexity and the need for extensive training data. Drawing inspiration from recent publications, the study adopts a focal network for training, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing the model's attention and optimizing emotional feature extraction. The proposed methodology aims to do the process of image emotion recognition by using the advantages of transformers while mitigating the computational problem associated with the deep neural networks. The incorporation of a focal network addresses attention-related challenges, and it contributes to the development of more efficient emotion recognition systems. This research offers insights into the evolving landscape of image emotion recognition methodologies and underscores the potential of transformer architectures in advancing this field.

articleTitle: Helmet Detection System Using Yolo V2
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: The risk of head injuries. The methodology The increasing concern for safety in a variety of work and leisure environments mandates the production of robust and efficient helmet detection systems. This study offers a fresh method for helmet detection, utilizing the (You Only Look Once version 2) YOLOv2 algorithm. The proposed system leverages the capabilities of YOLOv2 for real-time object detection, providing a proactive solution to enforce helmet-wearing regulations and mitigate impacts that encompass gathering of data, pre-processing, designing of the model architecture, training, and assessment. Results from experiments show the YOLO has achieved the greatest mAP success rate of 96.72%. How well the suggested approach works in precisely detecting helmets in diverse environments and scenarios. Furthermore, discussions on implementation considerations, challenges, and future research directions are provided, highlighting the potential impact of the helmet detection system on enhancing safety across industries and activities.

articleTitle: Enhancing IoT Object Tracking using Kalman Filter Algorithm in a Cloud Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: People tend to forget or misplace their valuable items and spend a lot of time finding them. An application capable of tracking lost items can be used as a solution. It would pinpoint the location of the object. Such an application is suitable for common people as well as for service companies. IoT and Cloud Computing technologies could be utilized to develop very reliable systems. Commonly used methodologies for finding location are the Velocity Renovation and Kalman Filtering process. These algorithms can work with applications like Google Maps on mobile devices. The system can extract the coordinates of the object and share them over SMS hence., location sharing feature is enabled too.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Insights: Personality Evaluation in Asynchronous Video Interviews for Informed Hiring Decisions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: An organization spends a lot of time and money on interviews. Asynchronous interviews can help businesses cut costs and save time. In order to be considered for a position, an applicant must understand both the hard and soft skills needed for the position. These can be set up in the system, and filtration for earlier rounds can be performed based on AI assessment algorithms. In this paper, we present algorithms for evaluating candidates' soft talents. This research paper presents a comprehensive exploration of machine learning algorithms, including Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest, Decision Trees, Logistic Regression, and XGBoost, as applied to personality assessment within the context of asynchronous video interviews. In the contemporary landscape of recruitment, asynchronous video interviews offer candidates a flexible platform to express themselves, transcending geographical constraints. We delve into the intricacies of the Big Five personality traits-openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroti-cism-and scrutinize the predictive capabilities of each algorithm in determining these traits from candidate responses. By incor-porating the optimal machine learning model into personality assessment, organizations can make more informed, data-driven hiring decisions, fostering the formation of high-performance teams while promoting equity and fairness in the recruitment process.

articleTitle: Lyrebird-Optimized PI Regulator for Enhanced Load Frequency Control in Two-Area Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: This paper introduces a groundbreaking approach to Load Frequency Control (LFC) in two-area interconnected power systems through the development of a Lyrebird-Optimized Proportional-Integral (PI) controller. The crux of this research lies in the innovative application of a novel optimization algorithm inspired by the lyrebird's exceptional mimicry capabilities, aimed at auto-tuning the PI controller parameters for improved system response to load variations. Traditional PI controllers, while prevalent for their simplicity, often fall short in dynamic environments due to the criticality of parameter tuning. The proposed Lyrebird-Optimized Algorithm (LOA) addresses this limitation by iteratively adjusting the PI parameters to find an optimal balance, significantly enhancing the system's stability and response characteristics. The proposed controller demonstrate superior performance in minimizing frequency deviations, reducing settling times, and maintaining system stability under varying load conditions. This study not only paves the way for more efficient and resilient power system operations but also opens new avenues for applying bio-inspired algorithms in complex engineering optimization problems.

articleTitle: Optimal Trained Ensemble of Classifiers for Brain Age Prediction Using MRI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: Prediction of brain age is necessary for a better understanding of the development of the human brain and ageing. Recently MRI data have been used for the estimation of brain age. However, variance in the development of brain age between the different as well as similar subjects gives variations in the developments at different ages. Therefore, advanced models are needed to predict brain age more accurately. Hence, this paper intends to propose an optimally trained ensemble classifier for brain age prediction by using MRI data. Initially, the MRI image is preprocessed by using the Bilateral Filtering process to eliminate the unwanted noise. Subsequently, the preprocessed images are segmented by the DBSCAN model and followed by feature extraction. Features such as LGBPHS, statistical features and pixel features are extracted from the segmented image. Finally, the prediction process is done via an ensemble classification model, which is a combination of RNN, Deepmaxout and GRU. Moreover, the weights of all the classifiers are optimally tuned by a proposed Self Improved-Bald Eagle Search Optimization (SI-BESO) to enhance its performance. The performance of the suggested ensemble model is evaluated over the conventional algorithms as well as classifiers in terms of performance measures like MAPE, MSE, MSLE, and MAE.

Author Keywords: Self Improved Bald Eagle Search Optimization

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition on Speech Attributes Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: Modern day technology is controlled by A.I. technology and new A.I. Voice generators are popular in today's world. However, the words we speak aren't always the information we want to communicate and hence, the emotion of the speaker plays an important role in determining the exact information the speaker is trying to communicate. It is important to solve such a problem since many legal as well as professional recordings could be analyzed properly and accurate outcomes could be inferred. The dataset will undergo a preprocessing which will give us a clean, no noise dataset which further will get split into two different parts, test and train. SVM, MLP, RF, DT algorithms were applied on the dataset to get insights on the information given to us. Speaker vocal tract information, represented by Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC), was extracted from the audio samples in the training dataset. Pitch, Short Term Energy (STE), and MFCC coefficients of audio samples in anger, happiness, fear, sadness like emotions were obtained. Then the nearest neighbor of unknown pitch, STE, and MFCC comparison for unknown data will decide the actual information on the data. The outcome must be validated and inferred for further references before deployment classifier algorithm came out to be most suitable for speech emotion recognition.

articleTitle: An Assessment Study on TV White Space in Nepal Using Low-Cost Spectrum Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: The examination of spectrum occupancy in distinct areas of Nepal is covered in this paper, with a focus on mobile and static data measurements to locate TV white spaces. The assessment was performed on the UHF band, particularly allocated for Digital Terrestrial TV (DTT) broadcasting bands in Nepal with static and mobile measurements. The data show significant changes in signal intensity across several frequency bands. According to mobile data measurement, the discussion emphasizes the high spectrum occupancy inside the valley, whereas stationary measurements offer a nuanced view of channel-specific occupancy. The analysis pinpoints specific frequency ranges with high potential TV white space or unused spectrum in various urban and rural locations of Nepal. Additionally, it emphasizes the importance of considering location-dependent spectrum intensity variations in resource allocation for broadcasting and communication purposes.

articleTitle: Hybrid CNN & Random Forest Model for Effective Mint Green Leaf Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: This investigation focuses on the automated identification the illnesses in minty green leaves utilizing a machine learning technique, specifically the CNN or Random Forest algorithms. The study's goal is to improve the accuracy and effectiveness of the disease detection in mint leaves, hence improving the general well-being and production of mint plants. The classification model was trained and tested on the large dataset containing the variety of illnesses such as the Mint Rust, Powdery Mildew, Mint Anthracnose, Verticillium Wilt, Green Spot illnesses, Downy Mildew, and Bacterial Leaf Spot. The analysis of the model's performance for each illness class, evaluation criteria such as Precision, Recall, F1-Score, Support, or Accuracy were used the results show that particular diseases have good precision, and recall, with F1-Score values ranging from 92.94% through 95.65%. The measures ‘Macro Average,’ ‘Weighted Average,’ or ‘Macro Average’ provide the additional aggregated insights into the overall model performance, producing consistently high scores of 94.27% throughout precision, recall, or FI-Score. The measure ‘Support’ represents the model's robustness, exhibiting significant cases for each illness class. The results of this study demonstrate the efficacy of the suggested machine-learning method for correctly categorizing illnesses in the mint leaves. The model's strong precision and recall scores validate its capacity to identify the particular illnesses, which aids in the early detection and tailored therapy.

articleTitle: Leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks for Classifying Lymphoma Using Histopathological Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: The lymphatic system serves as the origin of lymphoma, a cancerous condition in which lymphocytes undergo a malignant transformation and begin to divide uncontrollably. As the medical experts need more time to determine the type of lymphoma based on the histopathologic images. We used CNNs for the classification of lymphomas. In this work, we used the Multi Cancer Dataset for image classification. The Multi Cancer Dataset contains lymphoma images categorized into 3 classes and contains 15000 images with a size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{512}\times \mathbf{512}$</tex> pixels. Here we used a customized pre trained model to classify the images. We achieved accuracy of 96.2% and sensitivity of 96.2% in classifying lymphomas on histopathology images using the customized pre trained model. The preliminary results show how CNNs can be used to achieve a strong and correct classification of lymphomas, making them quite useful as an aid in histopathologic diagnosis.

articleTitle: Emotion Detection Based on Text and Emojis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: Opinion mining has become increasingly vital in today's digital world for making strategic decisions. With the volume of information increasing daily at a fast pace it becomes necessary to refine the information to efficiently analyze important and very vital data. Analysis of text to extract the emotions that are conveyed is a very important task, as analysis of text manually is time-consuming as well as may contain errors. Emojis have played a significant role in the digital world for communication and conveying various opinions. To solve these challenges an emotion detection model is introduced, that aims to address the issues related to accuracy of recognizing emotions by combining textual data and emojis. This model aids in various fields like sentiment analysis, mental health monitoring, feedback assessment. This research begins its journey by the creation of a diverse data set that contains text-based content that are meticulously labeled. To prepare the content in the data various preprocessing tasks are undertaken such as tokenization, removal of stopwords, normalization of text. The model is built in a recurrent neural network that is designed for managing multimodal input and trained through multi-label classification to predict the appropriate emotion category. Empirical formulas are referred to validate the model's effectiveness, which help in comparing the results obtained from text-only models in emotion recognition and emojis related sentiments. The aspects that set this model apart from the other models is its ability to adapt across platforms and languages, by recognizing the changing digital communication nature. As the nature of digital communication keeps on evolving it is necessary that various analytical tools are also evolved in parallel to address the changes as they come.

articleTitle: EmoSesnse-Automatic Speech Recognition Using AIML Implementation Through wav2vec2 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: The project, titled-“Emosense”, and very much like its name, leverages advanced machine learning algorithms to decode emotional cues embedded within speech patterns. By integrating sentiment analysis, tone detection, and contextual understanding, EmoSense discerns not only the words spoken but also the underlying emotions, empowering businesses to deliver personalised and empathetic responses This project is designed to analyse and classify human emotions from audio recordings of speech. It utilises the RAVDESS dataset, which contains a variety of emotional speeches from different actors. The data processing step involves loading and cleaning the dataset, and then extracting features from the audio files. The program then uses a deep learning model called Wav2Vec2 to convert the audio recordings into numerical representations. These representations are then fed into a classification model called “HubertForSequenceClassification” to classify the emotions. The program uses a tokenization process to convert the audio data into a format that can be fed into the model. The results of the model are visualised using graphs to show the accuracy and loss during the training process. The final accuracy of the model on the test dataset is 93 percent. The program's ability to accurately classify emotions from speech can provide valuable insights for various fields, including mental health, education, and entertainment. It can also be used to develop assistive technology for individuals with communication difficulties. The model's accuracy and ability to generalise to different speakers and accents can be further improved through additional training and fine-tuning. Overall, this program demonstrates the potential of deep learning models in speech emotion recognition and highlights the importance of developing accurate and robust models for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Qualitative Analysis of Homomorphic Encryption in Medical Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: The cloud computing revolutionized data processing and storage. The accessibility of cloud computing are the primary drivers of its rising use. The cloud is simple to use and accessible from any location in the world. Users or clients upload their data to the cloud, the cloud processes it, and they receive the intended outcomes. While cloud computing offers many advantages, it also exposes our private information to outside service providers. Sensitive patient medical history data that is maintained by numerous facilities is stored in the cloud for the medical industry. As a result, this information is kept as encrypted data. However, this data may also need to go through additional processing. Modern cryptography algorithms conduct actions on the decrypted data before re-encrypting it. Due to this, confidential information may be lost. Homomorphic encryption works on the encrypted data itself and provides the client with encrypted results. The paper examines and analyses the use of homomorphic encryption in the medical sector.

articleTitle: Image Description Generation using Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Overview
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: This survey paper explores the field of image description generation using deep learning, a critical intersection of computer vision and natural language processing. The paper provides a comprehensive overview of technical aspects, methods, datasets, and evaluation metrics relevant to image captioning. It delves into the challenges faced in automatically generating accurate descriptions for image content, emphasizing the importance of developing more effective methods in this domain. The integration of deep neural networks, specifically Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), is highlighted as a key enabler for achieving high-quality natural language descriptions of images. Various commonly used classification models and datasets are discussed, shedding light on the diverse range of approaches and resources available to researchers. Additionally, the paper presents a summary of reviewed research papers, showcasing the breadth and depth of advancements in image captioning and target recognition. It concludes with an invitation to future research, highlighting the vast potential and opportunities in this dynamic field.

articleTitle: Overstepping Existing Classifications: Deciphering Five Severity Tiers in Sugar Maple Tar Spot Disease Through Integrated CNN-GAN Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: This study classifies the Tar Spot disease severity of leaves from Sugar Maple using a large dataset of 7500 high-resolution images. Using transfer learning, the study deploys a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture and generative adversarial network (GAN) to analyze personally collected images. The developed model achieves an overall accuracy of 96.43%, which inhabits strong qualification in discriminating among the five severity levels. Performance metrics such as precision, recall, and specificity afford a more fine-grained assessment of the model's discriminative capacity for each severity class. A closer examination of the confusion matrix provides a glimpse into how good the model is at distinguishing between levels and points out where improvements are needed. Although it is based on a model with high accuracy, discussions point to the need for unceasing improvement to overcome the subtleties of disease processes and environmental influences. This research recognizes limitations and next steps. Although the model has huge potential in assessing the severity of Sugar Maple leaf disease, refinement is still needed to enhance its practical applicability for forestry management.

articleTitle: Twitter Data for Syndromic Surveillance: Insights and Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: Monitoring public health, vital for disease control, often relies on traditional surveillance methods. However, emerging approaches like syndromic surveillance offer the potential for early detection and rapid response to outbreaks. This paper explores the viability of Twitter data for syndromic surveillance, aiming to assess its timeliness and accuracy in detecting disease trends. The study sheds light on the challenges and opportunities in utilizing social media platforms for public health monitoring through rigorous investigation into data collection, preprocessing, and feature extraction techniques. Additionally, it delves into the nuances of keyword selection and language dynamics on Twitter, underscoring the need for adaptive strategies in data collection. The paper concludes with avenues for future research, including developing automated keyword selection algorithms and integrating geolocation data to enhance surveillance capabilities.

articleTitle: Productivity Analysis of Employees in Corporate Sector Using Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: In today's dynamic work environments, understanding and optimizing employee productivity are essential for organizational success. This paper introduces an approach for productivity analysis using gesture recognition techniques. By harnessing the capabilities of MediaPipe for body joint detection and LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) models for action classification, the proposed system enables real-time detection of employee actions. These actions are categorized into four key behaviors: nodding, showing interest, yawning, and resting. Additionally, a mathematical model is introduced to compute overall productivity based on these categorized actions. Moreover, the distribution of actions over time is visualized using graphs, providing valuable insights into employee behavior patterns and facilitating informed decision-making for productivity optimization.

articleTitle: From Data to Dialogue: Building a Domain-Agnostic Conversational Question Answering System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: In the realm of natural language processing (NLP), the quest for domain-specific question answering has been a focal point, emphasizing the precise extraction of factual information from designated knowledge sources in response to targeted inquiries. This project introduces a versatile, adaptable open-domain question answering system primed for seamless integration across diverse sectors, including educational institutions, e-commerce platforms, and healthcare portals. Leveraging the prowess of BERT and TAPAS, augmented with RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), our system offers a holistic solution catering to varied information retrieval needs. Through fine-tuning on domain-specific datasets, both BERT and TAPAS capitalize on their respective strengths: BERT's contextual understanding and TAPAS's structured reasoning capabilities. The ensemble model dynamically selects the most suitable approach for each query, ensuring flexibility in handling diverse linguistic nuances and query types. Moreover, the system integrates language translation and voice output features to further enhance its adaptability. Evaluation on benchmark datasets reaffirms the system's efficacy in delivering precise and coherent responses, underscoring its potential as a multifaceted tool for enhancing user interaction and information retrieval across educational, ecommerce, healthcare, and other domains.

articleTitle: Polycystic Ovary Syndromedetection via Hybrid Model with Improved Resampling Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: PCOS is a kind of malfunction of endocrine, which affects the reproductive system of females. This disorder degrades the chance of pregnancy. The major cause of this disorder is the suspicious increase of the male hormone named antrogen in the female body. The abnormal function of this antrogen affects the naturally present hormones of females. Various symptoms of PCOS are abnormal menstrual cycle, over-bleeding in menstrual time, acne, excessive weight, and sometimes this may lead to serious health problems such as ovarian cancer, and type 2 diabetes. Early detection of PCOSmay control this disorder. Accordingly, this work introduces a hybrid model with an improved re-sampling method for the detection of PCOS, which includes five processes. They are preprocessing, data sampling, data augmentation, feature extraction and detection. The data normalization is carried out in the preprocessing of data, which enhances the quality of the dataset for better analysis. Subsequently, proposing an improved SMOTE framework for sampling the dataset. The sampled data be augmented using a min-max data augmentation process. Subsequently, various features like entropy-based features, statistical features and mutual information-based features are extracted. Finally, a hybrid classification model is used for the classification process, which comprises BiGRU and a deep maxout classification model. Finally, the performance of the proposed work is evaluated in terms of different metrics.

articleTitle: Attention on Emotions: A Vision Transformer Approach to Advancing Facial Expression Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: “Progress in facial emotion recognition (FER) is essential for improving interactions in affective computing, social robots, and human-computer interface systems. Although the foundation for FER was established by conventional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), recent developments in computer vision have led to new opportunities using Transformer-based models, which have demonstrated exceptional performance in tasks such as picture classification and semantic analysis. In the framework of an extensive FER dataset, we test the performance of many Vision Transformer (ViT) models in addition to well-known CNNs like MobileNet and DenseNet. With the help of the FER2013 dataset, which is well-known for its varied portrayal of face expressions in grayscale pictures, we used several data augmentation methods to replicate real-world diversity. By using careful training with optimized parameters for both CNN and ViT models, our work provides a comparison analysis that shows the advantages and differences between each model type for FER tasks. This investigation shows that CNNs are still useful for effectively processing face characteristics and supports the viability of ViTs in capturing complex emotional expressions. Our results provide important new understandings of the features of the model that provide precise emotion identification, paving the way for further advancements in emotion-aware systems in a variety of fields.”

articleTitle: A Meticulous Analysis of Diverse Human Traits in Avid Readers and Non-Readers Through Advanced Data Analytics and Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: In the contemporary digital landscape, the enduring practice of reading books encounters formidable challenges amidst the pervasive allure of instant digital gratification. This paper embarks on a nuanced exploration, dissecting the intricate interplay between digital culture and the enduring significance of reading. While past research has predominantly scrutinized the dwindling popularity of reading and its repercussions on empathy and academic performance, our study takes a deeper dive. We focus on scrutinizing the ramifications of reading, or its absence, on pivotal aspects including stress levels, sleep quality, memory, and cognitive functions. Through rigorous comparative analysis between avid readers and non-readers, our aim is to elucidate the comprehensive impact of reading on human well-being. Furthermore, as part of our research endeavor, we intend to employ sophisticated machine learning models to predict an individual's psychological profile, particularly focusing on their position within the psychology spectrum. Leveraging cutting-edge sophisticated machine learning techniques and data visualization techniques, this research endeavors to unravel the subtle connections between reading habits and diverse dimensions of well-being, underscoring the paramount importance of nurturing a steadfast reading habit.

articleTitle: Accuracy Enhance of Smart Energy Theft Detection Using Machine Learning Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: Many operational losses occur throughout the generation, transmission, and distribution of electrical energy. Technically, we can quantify generating losses, but distribution and transmission losses cannot be precisely calculated using sending end information. To overcome these drawbacks, Accuracy Enhance of Smart Energy Theft Detection Using Machine Learning Classifiers is proposed in this paper, which makes use of machine learning based implementation for its operation. Specifically, electricity board can get the energy consumption statistics instantly on alert message Furthermore, whenever a consumer tries to theft electricity, current sensors trigger sending suitable signals to the microcontroller, which then transmits theft event messages to the algorithms side for further processing. After a theft is detected, the output will appear as an alert message after five counts of thefts. The Naive Bayes model outperforms the Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Simple Logistic models in terms of accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and score, and it has the lowest miss rate. The number of features also effects the model's classification and prediction skills.

articleTitle: Optimizing Microgrid Performance Using Transient Droop Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: The adoption of microgrids as decentralized energy systems has gained substantial momentum in recent years due to their potential to enhance energy resilience, reduce carbon emissions, and improve grid reliability. Central to the successful operation of microgrids is the implementation of advanced control strategies, with droop control emerging as a key technology. This project's primary objective is to investigate and optimize microgrid performance by using droop control operations. The project explores how droop control can adapt to varying load conditions and grid disturbances, ensuring uninterrupted power supply and stability. By implementing and testing the optimized droop control system in a real-world microgrid environment, this project seeks to demonstrate tangible improvements in microgrid performance, energy efficiency, and the ability to integrate renewable resources seamlessly.

articleTitle: DevOps Dynamics: Tools Driving Continuous Integration and Deployment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: In the ever-evolving landscape of software development, the integration of development and operations (DevOps) practices has become instrumental for achieving agility, collaboration, and rapid delivery. This paper provides an in-depth analysis and review of various DevOps tools that facilitate continuous integration, deployment, and collaboration within software development teams. The study explores the features, strengths, and limitations of prominent tools in the DevOps landscape. This paper delves into the dynamic realm of DevOps, with a specific focus on the tools that steer continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) processes. Through an extensive examination of key DevOps tools, their functionalities, and real-world applications, this research aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of how these tools contribute to the seamless integration of code changes, automated testing, and continuous delivery. By exploring the nuances of popular DevOps tools, the paper aims to empower software practitioners, teams, and organizations with insights to make informed decisions about tooling choices, fostering a culture of efficiency, reliability, and innovation in the software development lifecycle.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Ovarian Cancer Diagnosis: A ResNet50 Approach for Precision Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: The abstract functions as a short explanation of the study's goals, procedures, findings, and conclusions. We intended to create a robust machine learning model that could accurately identify different subtypes of ovarian cancer, like endometrioid carcinoma (EC), clear cell carcinoma (CC), mucinous carcinoma (MC), high-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC), and low-grade serous carcinoma (LGSC). In this model, powerful image processing algorithms and feature extraction methodologies are applied to identify certain key morphological and textural traits indicative of every subtype and leverage a collection of histology images of ovarian tissue samples. The generated model achieves an overall accuracy of 75%, which indicates the utility of the provided strategy. To establish the model's classification skills across numerous subtypes, we carried out a full evaluation of its performance, including measurements of accuracy, recall, and F1-score. This model indicates possible areas for growth, future research prospects, and the model's strengths or demerits. In summary, this work demonstrates the ability to identify ovarian cancer subgroups. It delivers insightful information that could boost the accuracy or precision of diagnosis to drive the formulation of tailored treatment regimens. The literature offers effective diagnoses on the utilization of computational approaches for increased accuracy, and the treatment continues to rise.

articleTitle: NLP-Driven Malware Classification: A Jaccard Similarity Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: Malware classification is a critical task in cybersecurity, essential for identifying and mitigating threats. This paper presents an approach to malware classification using Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques coupled with Jaccard similarity. We propose utilizing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n-\mathbf{grams}$</tex> of API call sequences, comprising API names and their arguments, to represent the behavior of malware samples. By computing the Jaccard similarity between these <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n-\mathbf{grams}$</tex>, we can effectively capture the similarities and differences in malware behavior. Our experiments reveal that different <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n-\mathbf{grams}$</tex> exhibit varying classification abilities, with some performing better for specific types of malware. Moreover, we observe that increasing the value of n in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n-\mathbf{grams}$</tex> leads to improved evaluation metrics, indicating the effectiveness of our approach. Overall, our method offers a promising approach to malware classification, leveraging NLP and Jaccard similarity to enhance accuracy and effectiveness in identifying malware variants.

articleTitle: Enhancing Implant Communication and a Design of a Wearable Flexible Antenna for Ultra-Wideband On-Body Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: An implanted microstrip patch antenna that has been enhanced for biological applications is described in this article. By utilizing a microstrip line feeding technique and a Rogers material substrate, the antenna's dimensions are optimized. This increases bandwidth, gain, and directivity. The simulation results indicate that the suggested configuration effectively facilitates wireless communication between implanted medical devices and additional systems. For a comprehensive evaluation, critical elements including gain, bandwidth, return loss, and directivity are examined and systematically organized in a table. Biomedical communication technology is advancing due to the new antenna design; consequently, medical implant wireless communication systems that are more dependable are imminent.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Model for Abnormalities Detection in Upper Extremity Radiographs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: Treating injuries by manual diagnosis of bone fractures in the upper extremities that are shoulder, humerus, elbow, wrist, finger, hand and forearm is a challenging task that can be prone to errors due to factors such as radiologist fatigue and experience level. For an accurate diagnosis and prompt treatment, anomalies of the upper extremities must be automatically detected in medical X-ray pictures. This research uses the MURA dataset to present a hybrid deep learning technique for multiclass categorization of anomalies in the upper extremity, encompassing the wrist, humerus, and elbow. This study uses pretrained Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) such as Visual Geometry Group (VGG19), Dense Convolutional Network (DenseNet121), and Residual Network (ResNet50), as well as customized CNN architectures, to classify abnormalities in upper extremity radiographs. These models are tailored to the anomaly detection job using transfer learning, resulting in accurate abnormality identification and localization. Furthermore, heatmap visualization techniques are used to improve anomaly identification outcomes, giving clinicians interpretable data for analyzing probable abnormalities in X-ray pictures.

articleTitle: Analysis of Improved Algorithm for Digital Filtering in Micro controller System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: In order to solve the challenge of improved algorithm analysis of digital filtering in single-chip microcomputer system, in view of the shortcomings of the existing clustering analysis algorithms, an improved algorithm analysis method based on D-P algorithm based on D-P algorithm is introduced. This new scheme uses the principle of overlapping sub-problem theory to accurately identify and locate the key influencing factors, and accordingly carries out a wise classification of indicators to reduce possible interference. At the same time, using the unique mechanism of the D-P algorithm, the proposed scheme cleverly constructs an improved design strategy for digital filtering. The empirical results show that the proposed scheme shows a significant improvement compisd with the traditional clustering analysis algorithm in terms of the accuracy of the analysis of the improved algorithm of digital filtering, the processing efficiency of key factors and other key performance indicators, showing its obvious strong advantages. In the MCU system, the improved algorithm analysis of digital filtering plays a vital role, which can accurately predict and optimize the growth trend and output results of the improved algorithm analysis of the digital filtering of the MCU system. However, in the face of complex simulation tasks, traditional clustering algorithms show some inherent shortcomings, especially when dealing with multi-level challenges, their performance is often unsatisfactory. To overcome this problem, this study introduces a new idea of improved algorithm analysis of digital filtering optimized by D-P algorithm, and accurately controls the influencing parameters through the overlapping sub-problem theory, which is used as the road map for index allocation, and then uses the D-P algorithm to innovate and construct a system scheme. The test results clearly point out that in the context of the evaluation criteria, the new scheme has been significantly optimized in terms of accuracy and processing speed for a variety of challenges, showing stronger performance superiority. Therefore, in the analysis of the improved algorithm of digital filtering of single-chip microcomputer system, the simulation scheme based on D-P algorithm successfully overcomes the shortcomings of traditional clustering analysis algorithms, and significantly improves the accuracy and operation efficiency of simulation.

articleTitle: Multiclass Kiwi Leaf Disease Detection Using CNN-SVM Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: This paper shows a new way to tell the difference between healthy and sick leaves on kiwifruit, which can help doctors correctly identify several leaf diseases. The system checks how well it can tell the difference between the different states of kiwi leaves by using several metrics, such as accuracy, recall, and F1-score. The results show that the method can correctly tell the difference between healthy and unhealthy leaves. It turns out that a lot of the following groups are correct: Pseudomonas syringae pv. actinidiae (Psa) (96.00%), botrytis blight (95.92%), anthracnose (94.90%), rust (95.79%), and healthy leaves (96.26%). Not only that, but the memory rate for each group shows that it can also spot real cases of each disease: healthy leaves (94.74%), rust (96.30%), anthracnose (95.38%), Botrytis blight (96.41%), Phomopsis leaf blight (94.96%), and Pseudomonas syringae pv (94.96%). it has actinidiae (Psa) (96.48%). The computer did exceptionally well across all of the classes, as shown by its F1 score, which serves as a measure of accuracy and memory. Finding diseases and telling the difference between healthy and sick leaves was very good for all five classes: rust (96.04%), anthracnose (95.14%), botrytis blight (96.16%), Phomopsis leaf blight (96.20%), and Pseudomonas syringae pv. actinidiae (Psa) (96.24%). Between the wide, weighted, along micro scores, the total grades show that it is right 95.88% of the time. So, this means that success is a strong and reliable factor in every field. Following these results, it becomes apparent that the algorithm can find problems with kiwi leaves or figure out what kinds of diseases those leaves had. Besides that, they show how the system can be used to help farmers deal with sickness and make sure crops get the care they need.

articleTitle: Fusing CNN and Random Forest for Predictive Modeling of Forging Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: In the abstract, This research article addresses the essential issue of forging flaws in manufacturing processes by implementing an advanced categorization model. The model uses Convolutional Neural Networks, or Random Forest techniques to accurately detect and categorise various forging flaws such as Fold, Scale, Underfill, Overflow, Upsetting Defect, or Seams. The model's performance is evaluated using accuracy, recollection, and F1-score measures for every defect class, and the results are extraordinary. Precision ratings vary between 96.77% to 97.36%, indicating the model's ability to minimize false positives. Recall values of 96.83% to 97.32% demonstrate the model's ability to capture real positive events while minimizing false negatives. The F1-score, a standardized indicator of precision and recall, is consistently greater than 97%, demonstrating a fair trade-off between precision with sensitivity for each fault class. The support values, which indicate actual examples of every category in the data set, range from 1235 through 1330, demonstrating that the dataset is diverse and representative. The support proportion, which ranges from 0.16 to 0.17, offers information on the relative prevalence of each fault type. With a total precision of 99%, the algorithm demonstrates remarkable skill in automating the identification of forging flaws. The macro-average, weighted-average, all micro-average scores all equal 97.07%, indicating consistent performance across classes and evaluation parameters. This research advances flaw detection approaches in manufacturing, guaranteeing the manufacture of high-quality forged parts with increased safety, dependability, and economic feasibility.

articleTitle: Analytical Framework for Stage-Based Classification of Female Alopecia: CNN-SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: This research paper presents the findings of a hair loss classification model that uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Support Vector Machines (SVMs) to categorize women's various innovative stages of hair loss. Four distinct classes-Type I, Type II, Type III, and Type IV-have their classification performance rigorously evaluated using metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, support, and support percentage. By accurately categorizing positive instances within each class, the model shows promise (accuracy values ranging from 98.25% to 98.73%). The model's recall metrics, which span from 98.31% to 98.68%, show how effectively it distinguishes positive scenarios from real-world ones. Furthermore, the F1-scores, which span all courses and have an average of 98.49% and encompass accuracy and recall, demonstrate constant performance. The analysis of support proportions highlights a balanced distribution of cases across classes, enhancing the robustness and relevance of the model. The model is effective in differentiating between alopecia phases, as seen by its weighted average accuracy of 98.50%. These findings highlight the amazing potential of the CNN-SVM technique to transform dermatological treatments via precise and automated classification of hair loss stages, improving patient outcomes and therapy as well as economic growth.

articleTitle: Synergizing CNN-SVM Models for Unified Recognition of Ladyfinger Leaf Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: In this paper, researchers describe a machine learning model developed to accurately classify diseases affecting ladyfinger leaves. A comprehensive dataset comprising 4380 photos serves as the foundation for the methodology. This dataset offers a diversified depiction of the situations that Ladyfinger leaves in. The model's performance metrics, which are reported in the table that follows, demonstrate remarkable precision, recall, and F1-Score values for a variety of illnesses, including Powdery Mildew, Cercospora Leaf Spot, Fusarium Wilt, Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus, and Bacterial Blight. All of these values are higher than 96.39%. The support values of the dataset provide evidence that it is a balanced representation, which in turn improves the model's ability to generalize. It is of particular significance that the model has a great overall accuracy of 96.57%, which demonstrates its dependability in accurately classifying diseases that affect ladyfinger leaves. A further demonstration of the model's consistently strong performance across a variety of evaluation parameters is provided by the macro, weighted, and micro averages. This research makes a significant contribution to the field of automated plant disease identification, illustrating the potential impact that machine learning could have on the advancement of agricultural methods. Because of the excellent accuracy and precision values that have been established, this model is a potential tool for farmers. It provides a dependable method for early disease identification and intervention, which ultimately contributes to the implementation of sustainable crop management techniques.

articleTitle: Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Classification Using STM32 Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a degenerative joint illness depicted by worsening of cartilage, resulting in pain, stiffness, and reduced mobility. Early prediction of knee OA prevents knee replacement and is essential for personalized treatment. This paper presents a deep learning based system for the computerized prediction of knee OA using clinical imaging data(X-rays). Key features extracted from imaging are utilized to train and validate the models, enabling accurate prediction of knee OA progression. For this KOA datasets with 3 grade classes (normal, moderate, severe) are trained and tested with MobileNetV1, EfficientNetBO0, Xception, DenseNet201, VGG16 and finally suggesting a high efficiency algorithm, which will be deployed on STM32 microcontroller through edge impulse. A comprehensive analysis will be taken which includes latency, ROM, RAM, accuracy taken in edge impulse with stm32 and the efficient algorithm that was trained and tested using traditional method will be compared and thus we can obtain results of KOA severity level in reduced time and computation.

articleTitle: Cluster Shape Detection Using Dual Attention Induced Convolutional-Clustering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: Cluster shape detection holds a crucial role in the realms of data analysis, image processing, and pattern recognition, acting as a linchpin for revealing concealed structures and relationships within datasets. This study introduces an innovative approach, the Dual Attention Induced Convolutional-Clustering (DAICC) algorithm, to address cluster shape detection. The uniqueness of this approach lies in its distinctive feature extraction methodology, consisting of two key modules. The first module employs an attention mechanism that accentuates features across both spatial and channel dimensions within the feature space. Subsequently, a convolution operation in the second module abstracts high-level features. Following feature extraction, a Fuzzy C-means clustering approach categorizes data points into distinct clusters. Subsequent to the clustering process, a novel algorithm for cluster shape detection is employed. This algorithm is characterized by its simplicity, computational efficiency, and effectiveness in identifying the shapes of clusters. Performance analysis underscores the superior efficacy of the proposed technique compared to state-of-the-art methods. This innovative approach holds promise as a valuable tool for iden-tifying cluster shapes in diverse applications, including image segmentation, medical fields (such as discerning the shapes of different microbes), and architectural contexts (e.g., identifying various aspects of urban structures).

articleTitle: Fusing CNN and XGBoost for Accurate Collard Green Variety Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: This study shows a new way to make the sorting of collard green types more exact across three categories Vates, Champion, and Georgia Southern. This is done by combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). The suggested mix uses the best parts of both CNN, known for pulling out features in picture data, and XGBoost - a strong way to improve the boosting method often used for sorting jobs. The set of information includes 12,000 pictures showing types of collard greens split into three different groups. The mixed model starts with the first part, CNN. This part pulls out detailed parts from the pictures put in it and takes note of all kinds of patterns linked to lots of different types and classified stuff that could be green leaves for eating or cooking purposes like cabbage or kale by looking at how deep their shades turn when cooked slowly without adding water too soon. Then, the taken-out parts are put into the XGBoost sorter. It smartly brings these together to make more careful guesses. The suggested plan not only helps in making progress with different types of collard greens but also could be useful for more uses in farming studies and careful farm work. This mixed method lets the model use the best parts of deep learning and gradient boosting, making it better at sorting things. Tests showed that the CNN-XGBoost mix model is more exact at 98.58% than just using CNN or XGBoost on their own.

articleTitle: Enhanced Total Hormonic Distortion in a Hybrid Microgrid with Fuel cells and Photovoltic Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: The outcome of this paper is to improve and enhance the power quality of the hybrid DC/AC microgrid (MG). The photovoltaic (PV) system and the proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) are used as renewable energy sources to deliver the optimum active power to the utility grid. The MG system based on the PV system, PEMFC and voltage source inverter is modelled mathematically. The proposed inverter is controlled using synchronous reference frame theory, called the direct-quadrature (dq) control method. Voltage Source Converter (VSC) helps to maintain the output voltage by enforcing the implementation of Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT). The maximum power point tracking which is used to step-up the voltage from the initial voltage from source. Total Hormonic Distortion of Output current is 1.3%. Here we are using the Fuzzy Logic controller, by using 7*7 Rules, we are improving the THD value of output current is 1.36%.

articleTitle: LTC-AE: Liquid Time Constant Autoencoders for Time Series Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: This research introduces a novel class of autoencoders, termed Liquid Time-Constant Autoencoder (LTC-AEs), for anomaly detection in time series data. Anomaly detection in real-time data streams is an extremely crucial task for various domains like healthcare, finance, and cyber security but it comes with a few challenges including missing values, class imbalances and noise. Recent research has proved optimal in addressing these challenges using sequential Autoencoders. Our proposed algorithm having the ability to capture temporal dynamics, learn from irregular sequences, improve interpretability and facilitate scalability, propose to help resolve some problems that delimits the potential of existing Autoencoder models. The experiments conducted in the study are utilized to emphasize the potential of our proposed model in handling multifaceted anomalies. The workflow follows semi-supervised learning to leverage the strengths of both supervised and unsupervised approaches. The utility of LTC-AEs are evaluated on various datasets and performance comparison is done with respect to architectures like Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM-AE), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU-AE) and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN-AE) Autoencoders.

articleTitle: Research on the Algorithm for the Design and Implementation of a 3D Visualization Platform for Tourism Resource Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: In order to meet the challenges of algorithm research on the design and implementation of 3D visualization platform for tourism resource management, in view of the shortcomings of the existing immunization algorithms, this study introduces an algorithm research method for the design and implementation of an innovative 3D visualization platform based on simulated annealing algorithm. This new approach uses the theoretical principles of the annealing process to precisely identify and locate the key influencing factors, and accordingly makes a sensible classification of indicators to reduce possible interference. At the same time, using the unique mechanism of simulated annealing algorithm, this scheme cleverly constructs a design strategy for the design and implementation of a 3D visualization platform. The empirical results show that this scheme shows a significant improvement comprised with the traditional immunization algorithm in terms of the accuracy of algorithm research and the processing efficiency of key factors in the design and implementation of the 3D visualization platform, showing its obvious strong advantages. In the management of tourism resources, the algorithm research of the design and implementation of the 3D visualization platform plays a vital role, which can accurately predict and optimize the growth trend and output results of the algorithm research of the design and implementation of the 3D visualization platform for tourism resource management. However, in the face of complex simulation tasks, traditional immunization algorithms show some inherent shortcomings, especially when dealing with multilevel challenges, their performance is often unsatisfactory. To overcome this problem, this study introduces a new idea of algorithm research for the design and implementation of a three-dimensional visualization platform optimized by simulated annealing algorithm, and accurately controls the influencing parameters through the annealing process theory, which is used as a road map for index allocation, and then uses the simulated annealing algorithm to innovate and construct a system scheme. The test results clearly point out that in the context of the evaluation criteria, the new scheme has been significantly optimized in terms of accuracy and processing speed for a variety of challenges, showing stronger performance superiority. Therefore, in the algorithm research process of the design and implementation of the 3D visualization platform for tourism resource management, the simulation scheme based on the simulated annealing algorithm successfully overcame the shortcomings of the traditional immunization algorithm and significantly improved the accuracy and operation efficiency of the simulation.

Author Keywords: simulated annealing algorithm;Oriented to tourism resource management;Design and implementation of 3D visualization platform;Algorithm research

articleTitle: The Performance of Interactive Genetic Algorithms in Digital Space Design in the Met Averse
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: In order to solve the challenge of the performance of digital space design under the met averse, in view of the shortcomings of the existing analog annealing algorithms, this study proposes an innovative representation method of digital space design based on interactive genetic algorithm. This new approach leverages the principles of natural evolutionary best theory to accurately identify and locate key influencing factors, and accordingly intelligently classify indicators to reduce potential interference. At the same time, using the unique mechanism of interactive genetic algorithm, this scheme cleverly constructs the design strategy of digital space design. The empirical results show that the proposed scheme shows a significant improvement compisd with the traditional analog annealing algorithm in the key performance indicators such as the accuracy of the digital space design and the processing efficiency of key factors, showing its obvious strong advantages. In the met averse, the performance of digital space design plays a crucial role, which can accurately predict and optimize the growth trend and output results of digital space design performance under the met averse. However, in the face of complex simulation tasks, traditional analog annealing algorithms show some inherent shortcomings, especially when dealing with multi-level challenges, their performance is often unsatisfactory. To overcome this, this study introduces a new idea of the performance of digital space design optimized by interactive genetic algorithm, and accurately controls the influencing parameters through the optimal theory of natural evolution, and uses it as a road map for index allocation, and then uses interactive genetic algorithm to innovate and construct a system scheme. The test results clearly point out that in the context of the evaluation criteria, the new scheme has been significantly optimized in terms of accuracy and processing speed for a variety of challenges, showing stronger performance superiority. Therefore, in the performance of digital space design under the met averse, the simulation scheme based on interactive genetic algorithm successfully overcomes the shortcomings of traditional analog annealing algorithms, and significantly improves the accuracy and operation efficiency of simulation.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Concrete Quality Optimization in Industry 4.0: Predictive Compressive Strength Modeling Through Machine Learning and Ensemble Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: As numerous manufacturing enterprises are progressing towards Industry 4.0, advanced predictive models are required to optimize contemporary construction practices. The precise prediction of the compressive strength of cement is crucial, as it is an integral material for any constructional unit. This research paper explores numerous advanced machine learning and ensemble learning techniques for effective concrete strength prediction, enabling proactive quality control measures in an Industry 4.0 based environment. The research utilizes an open-source dataset and employs advanced machine learning techniques to interpret and learn intricate relationships among input features, such as cement quantity, blast furnace slag content, fly ash ratios, water weight, superplasticizer usage, and coarse and fine aggregate proportions, as well as curing age for predictive modeling. Experimental results validate the Histogram-Based Gradient Boosting model as an optimal technique for effectivey forecasting the compressive strength of cement in Newtons per square millimeter (MPa), with a cross-validation R2 Score of 0.922. The findings of this research work contributes to the increasing demand for accurate and scalable predictive models within the quality control unit of an Industry 4.0 based manufacturing firm.

articleTitle: Video Activity Classification : A Comparative Analysis and Deep Learning Based Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: Video Activity classification is a fundamental task in computer vision with applications ranging from video surveillance, human-computer interaction to healthcare and autonomous robotics. Several techniques have been reported in the literature for the same. In recent years, Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have revolutionized the activity classification, enabling significant advancements in accuracy and robustness. This paper focuses on the deep learning techniques used for human activity detection and classification in videos. Previously statistical approaches were studied and employed for activity classification in which pattern recognition was majorly used. Recently, supervised learning based techniques are much utilized. This papers reviews the human activity recognition and classifying it with the use of video sequences and static images. The crucial steps in classifying the activities such as preprocessing, segmentation, frame extraction, feature vector extraction techniques, and classification models are also discussed. This paper provides a systematic survey of the state-of-the-art techniques, gaps between recent methods and methodologies in activity classification. The key challenges, datasets, and evaluation metrics are discussed throwing some light on the progress and future directions in the domain. Reviewing various surveys, the Long-Term Recurrent Convolutional Networks (LRCN) approach is implemented in this work. The implementation of LRCN approach shows that the model acquires an accuracy of 84.0476% on the action classes from the UCF-101 action datasets.

articleTitle: Enhancing Speech Emotion Recognition Through Advanced Feature Extraction and Deep Learning: A Study Using the RAVDESS Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: This study focuses on the significance of speech emotion recognition (SER) in facilitating the ability of machines to recognize and comprehend human emotions expressed through speech. This study introduces an innovative method for SER that incorporates sophisticated feature extraction techniques and deep learning approaches. The main objective is to improve the accuracy of identification, reduce processing requirements, and enable real-time application. Our suggested methodology utilizes the RAVDESS dataset and incorporates Mel-frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC) characteristics that are processed by a convolutional neural network (CNN) model. Our methodology has higher performance in comparison to baseline methods, as evidenced by extensive experimentation and analysis. The CNN model demonstrates successful generation of feature maps for the time series data, resulting in improved extraction and understanding of MFCC features. The effectiveness and robustness of our suggested approach are demonstrated by evaluation measures such as recognition accuracy, computing time, and real-time applicability. The superiority of our technique is further validated through comparative assessments with existing approaches, which confirm its genericity, accuracy, and dependability in various SER scenarios. The study's ROC diagrams offer visual substantiation of the model's efficacy in accurately classifying emotions across diverse emotion categories. This study not only makes a valuable contribution to the progress of SER technology but also establishes the foundation for future investigations in this domain. The findings obtained from our research provide a foundation for the advancement of more advanced and efficient SER systems, which have wide-ranging ramifications in several fields such as human-computer interaction, sentiment analysis, mental health diagnostics, and other related areas.

articleTitle: An Efficient Approach for News Summarization using Map-Reduce and Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: The ability to effectively summarize news articles is crucial in effectively managing the vast amount of available information. This research presents a novel approach to news summarizing, utilizing the combined functionalities of MapReduce and clustering methodologies. The limitations of traditional methods become apparent when faced with the vast and varied nature of news material, resulting in less-than-optimal summarizing results. The methodology employed in this study involves utilization of the MapReduce architecture for the simultaneous processing of extensive textual data. During the Map phase, summaries are generated in an independent manner by dividing news articles into smaller, more manageable segments. The final phase of clustering improves the process of summarization by grouping sentences that are semantically similar inside each chunk. This innovative methodology guarantees not only the capacity for expansion but also an enhanced capability to encompass a wide range of elements present in the original news content. The effectiveness of the suggested MapReduce and Clustering Summarization methodology is demonstrated through experiments conducted on CNN-daily dataset. Our research findings demonstrate enhancements in the quality of summarization, the speed of processing, and the capacity to manage larger datasets in comparison to traditional approaches. We were successfully able to make use of ideas of distributed computing and clustering algorithms which allowed us to generate news summaries that are all-inclusive as well as relevant in their contextual understanding. Our main aim of this research is to dig deep through the application of Map Reduce and clustering methodologies in field of news summarization within a research context.

articleTitle: Neural Network Based on Deep Learning Algorithm for Financial Management Early Warning Optimization Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: In order to solve the challenges of the neural network financial management early warning optimization model, in view of the shortcomings of the existing Grey correlation degree algorithm, this study introduces an innovative financial management early warning optimization model method based on deep learning algorithm. This new approach leverages neuronal theory principles to precisely identify and locate key influencing factors, and accordingly performs a sensible classification of indicators to reduce possible interference. At the same time, by using the unique mechanism of deep learning algorithm, this scheme cleverly constructs the design strategy of financial management. The empirical results show that this scheme shows a significant improvement compisd with the traditional gray correlation algorithm in terms of the accuracy of the financial management early warning optimization model and the processing efficiency of key factors, showing its obvious strong advantages. In neural networks, the financial management early warning optimization model plays a vital role, which can accurately predict and optimize the growth trend and output results of the financial management early warning optimization model of the neural network. However, in the face of complex simulation tasks, traditional grey correlation algorithms show some inherent shortcomings, especially when dealing with multilevel challenges, their performance is often unsatisfactory. To overcome this problem, this study introduces a new idea of financial management early warning optimization model optimized by deep learning algorithm, which accurately controls the influencing parameters through neuronal theory, and uses it as a road map for indicator allocation, and then uses deep learning algorithm to innovate and construct a system scheme. The test results clearly point out that in the context of the evaluation criteria, the new scheme has been significantly optimized in terms of accuracy and processing speed for a variety of challenges, showing stronger performance superiority. Therefore, in the process of financial management early warning optimization model of neural network, the simulation scheme based on deep learning algorithm successfully overcomes the shortcomings of the traditional gray correlation algorithm, and significantly improves the accuracy and operation efficiency of the simulation.

articleTitle: Wind Speed Probability Density Forecast Using Optimization Based Kernel Density Estimation and Quantile Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Information Technology, Electronics and Intelligent Communication Systems (ICITEICS)
abstract: In the past few decades, wind power has experienced significant progress. A number of nations have achieved a significant operational wind power capacity, while others are developing at rapid speeds in their wake. Power system management presents a challenge when integrating wind power on such a wide scale. Wind is, in fact, an unpredictable and fluctuating resource. For instance, extra reserves are typically set aside to handle this unpredictability. This reduces the advantages of employing such a RES supply and raises the total cost of the energy produced. Using forecasting technologies is one technique to lessen the uncertainty surrounding the production of wind power. These instruments are forecasting models with multiple steps forward, or look-ahead times, that offer data for multiple horizons. Most of the forecasting methods currently in use offer a single projected value for each prediction horizon known as deterministic, spot, or point forecasts. The primary disadvantage of these forecasts is that no information regarding deviations from the expected values is given. This restricts its application in scenarios involving decision-making, particularly those involving risk assessment or stochastic optimization. This research proposes a Quantile Regression (QR) and Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) based probability density forecasting system for wind speed. EMD is used to lower raw wind speed series noise. Furthermore, the de-noised wind speed signal is studied using both LQR and NQR models. Moreover, the KDE “bandwidth” and quantile regression random forest (QRRF) “numbins” are optimally tuned by means of an Adaptive Snake Optimization (ASO) process.
